# ContextMenu

A context menu: wraps any content and opens a menu of actions on right click, `Shift+F10` or the menu key, at
the pointer or next to the focused element. The menu is the Dropdown menu of the library.

**Interaction**: right click opens the menu at the pointer; `Shift+F10` or the menu key opens it below the
focused element. Focus moves into the menu: `↑` / `↓` move between items (skipping disabled items and
dividers), `Enter` runs one and `Esc` closes the menu; after closing, focus returns to the element that was
focused before. Clicking elsewhere closes it and leaves focus on the clicked element. Inside text fields the
browser's own menu (copy, paste) is kept. Shortcut hints are shown with Kbd.

**Category**: Basic · **Common uses**: Actions on list rows, files, images and messages, in the habits of desktop applications

## Import

```ts
import { ContextMenu } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

Right click a row, or focus it and press `Shift+F10` (or the menu key). The rows are focusable, so keyboard
users can open the menu too.

```tsx
export function Basic() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState('Nothing yet')
  return (
    <Stack gap={2}>
      <Stack gap={1}>
        {files.map((name) => (
          <ContextMenu
            key={name}
            onSelect={(key) => setLast(`${key}: ${name}`)}
            items={[
              { key: 'open', label: 'Open', icon: 'external-link' },
              { key: 'rename', label: 'Rename', icon: 'edit', shortcut: 'f2' },
              { key: 'copy', label: 'Copy link', icon: 'link', shortcut: 'mod+shift+c' },
              { type: 'divider' },
              { key: 'delete', label: 'Delete', icon: 'trash', danger: true, shortcut: 'delete' },
            ]}
          >
            <ListItem title={name} onClick={() => {}} />
          </ContextMenu>
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Text size="sm" tone="secondary">
        Last action: {last}
      </Text>
    </Stack>
  )
}
```

## States

### Disabled items and dividers

Disabled items are shown but skipped by `↑` / `↓`; dividers separate groups of actions. Each item can have an
`onClick` of its own.

```tsx
export function DisabledItems() {
  return <Card />
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly ContextMenuItem[]` | Menu items: actions (`key`, `label`, `icon`, `danger`, `disabled`, `shortcut`, `onClick`) and dividers (`{ type: 'divider' }`). With no items, the browser's own menu is shown. | — | Yes |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The content that has the menu: a list row, a file, an image, a message. For keyboard users, the content (or an element inside it) must be focusable. | — | Yes |
| `onSelect` | `(key: string) => void` | Called with the key of the chosen item, after its `onClick`. | — | No |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | Called when the menu opens or closes. | — | No |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Disables the menu: right click shows the browser's own menu. | — | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
